description: Composite five-panel figure combining synchrotron XRD line profiles, Modified Williamson–Hall (MWH) analyses and dislocation-density calculations for a carbon-free, austenite-based low-density steel containing δ-ferrite and hypereutectic TiB₂. (a) and (b) plot Intensity (a.u.) versus K (nm⁻¹) from 3 to 14 for the undeformed and the strained-to-fracture specimen respectively; peaks are indexed and colour-coded by an in-panel legend (δ-Ferrite black, Austenite blue, TiB₂ red), with the strongest reflection labelled 111 and others including 110, 200, 220, 311, 222, 331, 420, 422 plus a series of weak TiB₂ reflections (1010, 2110, 1012, 2020, 2112, 3030, 3031). Peak positions are essentially unchanged between (a) and (b) but the profiles broaden after straining. (c) and (d) are MWH plots of ΔK (nm⁻¹) versus KC̄^1/2 (nm⁻¹) for δ-ferrite (red) and austenite (blue) respectively, each showing filled-symbol 'Undeformed' and open-symbol 'Deformed' data with least-squares linear fits. (e) is a bar chart of dislocation density (10¹⁵ m⁻²) for Austenite and δ-Ferrite in the Undeformed and Deformed states, with error bars. Together the panels show ferrite starting with the higher dislocation density while austenite increases by roughly an order of magnitude on straining.

subfigures.description: Synchrotron XRD line profile of the undeformed sample: Intensity (a.u.) vs K (nm⁻¹) over 3–14 nm⁻¹. Sharp peaks are indexed and colour-coded by phase via an in-panel legend (δ-Ferrite black, Austenite blue, TiB₂ red); the tallest peak is labelled 111, with 110, 200, 220, 311, 222, 331, 420, 422 and multiple weak TiB₂ reflections.

The same K (nm⁻¹) 3–14 line profile for the sample after tensile straining to fracture, with the identical phase colour code. Peak positions match (a) but the reflections are visibly broadened; small red TiB₂ peaks remain at the same positions.

MWH plot for δ-ferrite: ΔK (nm⁻¹) from 0.02 to 0.08 versus KC̄^1/2 (nm⁻¹) from 1.5 to 5.0. Red filled squares = Undeformed, red open circles = Deformed, each set with a least-squares straight-line fit; the deformed (open-circle) data scatter more widely about their line.

MWH plot for austenite: ΔK (nm⁻¹) from 0.00 to 0.10 versus KC̄^1/2 (nm⁻¹) from 1.5 to 5.5. Blue filled squares = Undeformed, blue open circles = Deformed, each with a linear fit; the deformed set lies higher and its fit has the steeper slope.

Bar chart of dislocation density (10¹⁵ m⁻², axis 0–2.5) for Austenite (blue bars) and δ-Ferrite (red bars) in the Undeformed and Deformed conditions, with error bars; deformed bars are much taller than undeformed ones and carry larger error bars.

observations.observation: (a) plots Intensity (a.u.) against K (nm⁻¹) from 3 to 14 nm⁻¹ for the undeformed sample, with sharp peaks indexed and colour-coded by phase using an in-panel legend (δ-Ferrite black, Austenite blue, TiB₂ red).
(b) covers the same K (nm⁻¹) range with the same phase legend for the deformed sample; peak positions coincide with (a) but the line profiles are broadened after straining.

(c) is the MWH plot for δ-ferrite with ΔK (nm⁻¹) on the 0.02–0.08 axis and KC̄^1/2 (nm⁻¹) on the 1.5–5.0 axis; red filled squares are 'Undeformed', red open circles are 'Deformed', each with a straight-line fit.

(d) is the MWH plot for austenite with ΔK (nm⁻¹) on the 0.00–0.10 axis and KC̄^1/2 (nm⁻¹) on the 1.5–5.5 axis; blue filled squares are 'Undeformed' and blue open circles 'Deformed', and the deformed fit is steeper.

(e) is a dislocation-density bar chart (10¹⁵ m⁻², axis 0–2.5) with blue = Austenite and red = δ-Ferrite bars for Undeformed and Deformed; in the undeformed state the red (ferrite) bar is much taller than the blue (austenite) bar, whereas after deformation the blue bar reaches about 2 and exceeds the red bar.
The caption states that (a) is the undeformed sample and (b) the sample after tensile straining to fracture.
The caption states that (c) and (d) are MWH plots of δ-ferrite and austenite respectively and that (e) shows the evolution of dislocation density before and after straining for both phases.
The citing text states that each synchrotron XRD pattern yields nine (K, −K) data points for austenite and six for ferrite, fitted by least squares to ΔK versus KC̄^1/2.
The citing text states the initial dislocation density of ferrite is (1.1 ± 0.2)×10¹⁵ m⁻², higher than the (3 ± 0.7)×10¹⁴ m⁻² of austenite.
The citing text states that after plastic deformation the ferrite dislocation density rises slightly to (1.7 ± 0.7)×10¹⁵ m⁻² while austenite rises by an order of magnitude to (2 ± 0.3)×10¹⁵ m⁻².

The citing text states the error bars in (e) represent the standard deviation of the linear fitting slope from (c, d), and that the large uncertainty of the deformed δ-ferrite value comes from the comparatively weak linear relationship of the empty-circle data in (c).
The citing text states the initial dislocation density ρ0 taken from (e) was used, together with the tensile curves, to determine the crystal-plasticity parameters k1 and k2 in Table 1.

unreadable_items: panels (a) and (b): the cluster of small red TiB₂ peak labels is very compact and only partially readable; not every index could be confirmed independently of the caption
